scope: Device & materials: MRAM (Toggle, STT, SOT, eMRAM), ReRAM/memristor/CBRAM, PCM/3D XPoint — incl. design-in, defense-first, IP-licensing, salvage and software lenses

cards.name: Supercap-Killer PLP Kit (MRAM write-cache reference design)
cards.what_it_is: A licensed reference design (schematic/layout, FPGA or RISC-V controller RTL, Linux/Zephyr journaling driver, validation suite) that replaces the DRAM + supercapacitor power-loss-protection block in SSD, computational-storage, RAID/HBA and industrial data-logger boards with Everspin PERSYST 1Gb ST-DDR4 or 64-256Mb xSPI STT-MRAM. Parts come from Everspin (GF 28nm CMOS + Chandler AZ MTJ BEOL; Microchip Gresham OR line from 2H-2027); revenue is design-package fee + per-unit royalty + design-in services.
cards.why_it_could_work: IBM moved its 5th-gen FlashCore Module to Everspin MRAM instead of capacitors (Oct-2026) because supercaps/batteries wear out in a few years and take board space. The PLP block needs only 64-512 MB, so MRAM's ~30x $/bit penalty (~$100/Gb street vs ~$3/Gb DRAM) costs ~$50-400 per board but deletes the capacitor bank, hold-up circuitry and its field failures. DRAM write-cache cost doubled in 2026 while MRAM pricing did not move with the DRAM cycle, narrowing the delta. Everspin is adding U.S. capacity (Microchip 10-yr deal, up to 1,300 wafers/qtr).

cards.who_is_already_doing_this: Everspin application engineering (gives reference designs free), IBM (in-house FCM), Phison (controller support), Broadcom/LSI RAID (Everspin journal MRAM since 2012), Marvell/Microchip SSD controller reference boards
cards.wins_axis: lifecycle length and non-volatility of the write cache (no supercap aging), board area, PLP reliability — NOT $/GB
cards.buyer: Tier-2 enterprise/industrial and rugged/defense SSD makers, computational-storage startups, RAID/HBA card makers, flight/data-recorder and PLC OEMs with 10-20-year field life
cards.glut_reason: The reliability/supercap-elimination case is independent of DRAM price, but a 60% DDR5/DDR4 drop makes the DRAM+supercap alternative ~$20-50 cheaper per board, so marginal designs revert to DRAM.
cards.fatal_flaw: Everspin and the controller vendors already give this engineering away to win sockets, and the number of new PLP designs per year is dozens, not thousands — a kit business likely caps below ~$1M/yr; plus an ITC exclusion order on Everspin STT-MRAM (Avalanche, 337-TA-1487, ~mid-2027) could interrupt 1Gb supply.
cards.business_model_lenses: module/appliance (reference design), IP licensing (design package + royalty), design services, defense-first variant (rugged SSDs)
cards.founder_fit_note: Founder can own drivers, test tooling and sales, but needs a contract hardware/FPGA engineer (~$30-60k year 1); slow but possible alongside the day job.
cards.possible: yes — the mechanism ships today in IBM FCM5 and LSI RAID journals
cards.profitable: marginal — real but small niche; Everspin captures most of the value
cards.doable_by_founder: marginal — T1 and needs an EE partner; no fab, no chip design

cards.name: DDR3-EOL Socket Swap to ST-DDR4 MRAM
cards.subbranch: STT-MRAM as small-density DRAM replacement (industrial long-lifecycle)
cards.what_it_is: Redesign service and drop-in mezzanine that replace end-of-life 1-4Gb DDR3/DDR4 chips on long-lifecycle industrial, medical and rail controllers with Everspin 1Gb ST-DDR4 STT-MRAM (GF 28nm + Chandler BEOL), selling instant-on non-volatility as the bonus. Target boards that need <=256 MB of working memory.
cards.why_it_could_work: DDR3/DDR4 are being exited by Samsung/SK hynix/Micron in 2026 and DDR4 contract rose >50% QoQ in Q3-2026, so long-lifecycle OEMs face forced respins anyway; a respin to MRAM removes battery-backed SRAM/supercaps and gives a part with a 10+-year roadmap from a U.S. vendor. COMPUTED REALITY: MRAM street ~$100/Gb vs DDR3 4Gb spot ~$3.19/Gb = ~32x per bit; manufacturing cost ~$91/GB (MRAM, 28nm) vs ~$2.5-4.5/GB (DRAM). Doubling DRAM prices does not close a 30x gap.

cards.wins_axis: non-volatility + supply longevity (U.S. vendor roadmap) for boards needing <=256 MB
cards.buyer: industrial PLC, medical-device and rail-signalling OEMs with DDR3 EOL exposure
cards.glut_reason: In a glut DDR3/DDR4 last-time-buy and broker stock gets cheap and plentiful; the only reason to swap (forced EOL respin at shortage prices) disappears and the 30x bit-cost gap widens to ~100x.
cards.fatal_flaw: 30x $/bit gap, 1Gb max per MRAM die (a 1GB board needs 8 dies), and ST-DDR4 is not pin/protocol compatible with DDR3, so a respin to LPDDR4/DDR4 is cheaper for almost everyone.
cards.founder_fit_note: Cheap to start as a consulting offer, but needs hardware design skill the founder lacks and the economics rarely close.
cards.profitable: no — loses on $/GB by ~30x except in rare <=256 MB sockets
cards.doable_by_founder: marginal — consulting-only form is T0 but needs an EE

cards.name: NewSpace MRAM Radiation-Data & Upscreen Service
cards.what_it_is: Buy lot-traceable Everspin Toggle MRAM (MR4A16B, Chandler AZ) and PERSYST HR xSPI STT-MRAM (EM064LX) and run heavy-ion, proton and TID campaigns at U.S. beam facilities (e.g., Texas A&M Cyclotron Institute, LBNL 88-Inch BASE [names from training, UNVERIFIED access terms]), then sell (a) a subscription database of lot-specific radiation and screening results and (b) upscreened, serialized parts to LEO smallsat builders. Software platform (lot genealogy, test data, SEE rate calculators) is the founder's build.
cards.why_it_could_work: NewSpace demand is pulling non-volatile MRAM into orbit: Everspin's 64Mb HR xSPI reached full production on LEO demand and Astro Digital picked it for a GEO bus (Q2-2026). Toggle MRAM shows >1 Mrad(Si) TID (Frontgrade/Cobham). Smallsat builders cannot pay QML-V prices or wait 20-26-week lead times (EM064LX 20 wks, EM128LX 26 wks) and want lot-specific COTS+ data. A report sells for ~$5-25k [ESTIMATE]; screened parts carry 2-4x markup on ~$40-60 parts.

cards.name: New Fabless Discrete STT-MRAM Vendor
cards.subbranch: Discrete STT-MRAM chips (fabless on foundry eMRAM)
cards.what_it_is: Start a fabless U.S. company selling 128Mb-4Gb discrete STT-MRAM (CoFeB/MgO pMTJ) built on a foundry MRAM module (Samsung 28FDS/14nm, UMC 22nm or TSMC 16nm), competing with Everspin, Netsol and Avalanche in SPI/xSPI and ST-DDR4 sockets.
cards.why_it_could_work: Foundry eMRAM is now standard (Samsung 14/8nm cells 0.024/0.017 um2; GF AutoPro150; TSMC 16nm), so a fabless entrant needs no MTJ fab. COMPUTED: a 4Gb die at 14/16nm with a 0.024 um2 cell is ~229 mm2 and costs ~$72/GB — still ~3.6x the PEAK DDR5 contract price before margin — so the only markets are NOR/FRAM/nvSRAM replacement and PLP, which Everspin already serves.

cards.name: MRAM Main-Memory DIMM / CXL Module
cards.what_it_is: A persistent DDR4/DDR5 RDIMM or CXL Type-3 module populated with STT-MRAM dies (Everspin 1Gb ST-DDR4 today, hypothetical 4Gb 16nm dies later) sold as non-volatile main memory for servers during the DRAM shortage.
cards.why_it_could_work: Tempting because DRAM is 2-3x and MRAM is non-volatile with no refresh. COMPUTED KILL: Everspin 1Gb density 9.75 Mb/mm2 vs ~400 Mb/mm2 for 1b DRAM (~42x less silicon-efficient). A 32GB RDIMM needs 256 MRAM dies (~27,000 mm2) vs 16 DRAM dies (~640 mm2). Cost ~$91/GB (28nm) or ~$72/GB (16nm) vs DDR5 ~$20/GB peak and ~$8/GB glut; street MRAM ~$821/GB.

Chips price per part ($20-200 in defense), so the ~$3,300/GB bit cost is irrelevant. SBIR/STTR topics for trusted microelectronics can fund the design.

cards.name: 3D XPoint / PCM Crosspoint Revival for the CXL Memory Tier
cards.what_it_is: Rebuild Optane-class memory: Ge-Sb-Te phase-change (or OTS selector-only) cells in a 4-deck 20nm-half-pitch crosspoint, sold as CXL Type-3 persistent/capacity memory at a fraction of DRAM $/GB during the shortage.
cards.why_it_could_work: The math looks great in Nov-2026: XPoint Gen2 was 1.31 Gb/mm2 (~3.3x 1b DRAM density) and at full fab loading the die cost computes to ~$1/GB vs DDR5 at ~$20/GB. But Optane died anyway: Intel lost >$7B, took a $559M inventory write-off (Q2-2022); Micron cited 'insufficient market validation', booked ~$545M underutilization in 4 quarters and sold Lehi to TI for $900M (below book). The killers were volume (Lehi underloaded), an Intel-only DDR-T ecosystem, ~3-4x DRAM latency, and the 2019 DRAM glut erasing Optane's ~$6.6/GB price advantage. SanDisk + imec are now prototyping '3D Matrix Memory' (target ~half DRAM cost/bit, no dates).

cards.name: Optane PMem Salvage: Cheap Memory-Mode Capacity for Cascade/Ice Lake Fleets
cards.what_it_is: Buy decommissioned Intel Optane PMem 100/200 modules (128/256/512 GB, 3D XPoint Gen1 media) from U.S. ITAD/recyclers, health-test them (ipmctl SMART/percentage-used, burn-in), and sell validated kits plus a web sizing tool that configures Memory Mode or App Direct for VMware/KVM, SAP HANA, Redis and HPC nodes on 2nd/3rd-gen Xeon Scalable servers.
cards.why_it_could_work: DDR4 RDIMMs rose >50% QoQ in Q3-2026 and DDR4 is being exited, so owners of still-useful Cascade Lake/Ice Lake fleets cannot cheaply add memory. New PMem cost $6.6-11/GB in 2019 and Intel exited with ~2 years of excess XPoint inventory; recovered modules may trade at ~$0.8-2/GB [UNVERIFIED] vs DDR4 RDIMM ~$25+/GB. Memory Mode uses DRAM as cache in front of 4-8x more PMem capacity. Software (sizing, health certificates, config scripts) is the founder's edge.

cards.name: MRAM Persistent-Log Accelerator (nvNITRO revival)
cards.what_it_is: A PCIe/NVMe or CXL card carrying 2-4 GB of Everspin 1Gb ST-DDR4 MRAM behind an FPGA controller, sold as an ultra-low-latency, unlimited-endurance write-ahead-log device for ZFS SLOG, PostgreSQL WAL, Ceph/Kafka journals and trading logs.
cards.why_it_could_work: Optane P5800X/P1600X (the favorite SLOG/WAL devices) are discontinued, leaving a latency niche; MRAM has no supercap and near-unlimited endurance. But media BOM is ~$1,000-3,200 for 4 GB (32 x 1Gb at $30-100) vs ~$80 of DRAM + supercap, and SLC/XL-Flash SSDs plus surplus Optane cover most buyers. Everspin's own MRAM NVMe card (nvNITRO, ~2017) did not reach volume [UNVERIFIED: training].

cards.name: SOT-MRAM Last-Level-Cache Chiplet
cards.what_it_is: A UCIe-attached cache chiplet using spin-orbit-torque MRAM (beta-W/Ta SOT track under CoFeB/MgO MTJ, 2T1R) to replace SRAM last-level cache in AI accelerators at N5-class nodes.
cards.why_it_could_work: imec reports SOT switching <100 fJ/bit and >1e15 endurance (IEDM-2023) and a 2025 IEEE TED study shows BEOL read selectors shrink bitcells 10-40% toward sub-N3 SRAM area; multi-bit VGSOT claims ~3x SRAM density. COMPUTED: even at 0.03 um2 a 1Gb die is ~80 mm2 at ~$262/GB — an SRAM-replacement play, not a DRAM one.

cards.name: eMRAM-Unified-Memory Edge MCU (no external DRAM)
cards.what_it_is: A fabless edge-AI MCU on GF 22FDX+ with AutoPro150 eMRAM (alt: TSMC 22RRAM) holding 16-64 MB of weights and working data on-die so the board needs no external DRAM/PSRAM or NOR — a way to dodge the DRAM shortage in edge devices.
cards.why_it_could_work: Foundry eNVM is mature: GF AutoPro150 (Auto Grade 1, 500k cycles, <10ns read, volume 2H-2026 Dresden, PDK self-serve), TSMC 22RRAM (100K cycles), ST/Samsung 18nm ePCM (0.059 um2 cell, smallest). Removing an external LPDDR4 (now ~2x price) saves BOM and standby power.

cards.name: NVM-EOL Migration Finder (MRAM/FeRAM/ReRAM cross-reference SaaS)
cards.subbranch: Software tool for the shortage, grounded in emerging-NVM device data
cards.what_it_is: A web app that ingests lifecycle/PCN/EOL notices and distributor data (e.g., Renesas serial EEPROM EOL with last-time ship 2026-10-31, DDR3/DDR4 EOLs) and recommends pin- and protocol-compatible emerging-NVM replacements (Everspin Toggle/xSPI MRAM, FeRAM, Netsol MRAM, ReRAM-based parts) with BOM cost, lead-time (e.g., 20-26 weeks for Everspin xSPI) and qualification deltas; revenue from seats for component engineers plus referral fees from authorized distributors.
cards.why_it_could_work: 2026 is an EOL wave (DDR3/DDR4 exits, serial EEPROM EOLs) during a shortage, and emerging-NVM parts are under-known by component engineers. The founder can build it with no hardware capital; device knowledge from this branch becomes the data moat (density, endurance, interface compatibility).
